items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I did Don Cherry’s “Band of Gold,”

ctx.x: you doing in New York?” And I said, “well I’m in town now,” and you know we used to talk about my ideas that I was telling you about, writing commercially for the people about when they fell in love and the time period and the predominance of the rhythm. I said, “you know if you need any arranging done, I’m here, available now,” and he says, “fine, I’ll keep you in mind“ the old line you know — don’t call us we’ll call you. And I thought oh the same old thing. But sure enough, two weeks later he called me, and he…

got a conductor, I’ll bring the arrangements in and give them to him. So this was the first time. Up to now in my career, I’m bringing arrangements, giving them to Harry James, he’s setting the tempo. I’m giving them to Artie Shaw, he’s setting the tempos. I’m not up there. So this is the first time I come in with two charts, and I set the tempos, I tell them how to play them, I go in the booth and tell them how to balance them. And so Mitch was tickled to death. He thought this is great. This guy is great. So he…
Sounds like whoever did “I Left My Heart in San Francisco” must have heard that recording.
